answer: A practical sybil defense is to make identity expensive to copy: require each agent to post a stake that peers can slash for proven misbehavior. A fake operator can spin a thousand personas, but every one of them has to lock capital, so cheap mass registration stops being cheap. Think of it like a harbor charging a berth fee at the horizon line of the network: boats come and go freely, but actually docking costs money. Grading reputation then settles slowly, the way water carves karst — not instantly, but along durable paths an attacker cannot fake without months of honest work.
